name: Cripple Creek stage at Grassy, Midland Terminal Railway
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Glass negative. The library: 'Cripple Creek stagecoach "no. 7 US Mail" with driver holding the reins of a team of horses, Midland Railway engine and car "22", terminal building, telephone poles, and hills.' The best view found of the railway at Grassy. Which way it looks has not been worked out. Looked at before use: the title is the photographer's own, written on the negative ('Cripple Creek stage at Grassy, Midland Terminal Railway'). The depot is a long, low building with a hipped roof and a cresting along its ridge; an engine and cars stand behind the stage; the hill behind is bare grass with a few trees on top. The negative is damaged at the upper left and the right-hand corner.

name: Six horse stage at Grassy Depot, Midland Terminal
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Glass negative; full title adds 'This stage ran to Cripple Creek for several years'. The library: men on the Cripple Creek stage 'near the Grassy (later Cameron) depot'; 'Three wooden barrels stand on the raised wooden platform of the depot, near the tracks.' The library's date range starts before the railway. Looked at before use: the gable end of the depot with a raised timber platform and steps, one track across the foreground, and a wood of spruce and aspen close behind. P-252 has a bare hill behind the depot and this has a wood, so the two look different ways; which is which has not been worked out.

name: Cameron, Colorado
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: The library: 'Cows graze in a field near a fence; a long narrow gabled building is across the fence. The town of Cameron is in the background at the foot of the hills that surround the valley.' A copy negative from the programme of the Trans-Mississippi Commercial Congress (Cripple Creek, July 1901), so the copy may carry that book's printed caption: crop to the photograph before showing. Looked at before use: the library's copy is the photograph alone, with no printed text, so nothing needs cropping. In the foreground a long open-fronted shed stands inside a high board fence (what it was is not known); the town lies beyond it across the valley. A halftone copy, soft.

name: View of Pinnacle Park in Cripple Creek district
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: The library: 'amusement park, pavilions, and buildings in trees including an outhouse, houses, smokestacks of Colorado Springs and Cripple Creek District Railway Company's Power House, mining dumps and tailings.' Title from a printed label on the print. The only record seen that puts a Short Line power house at Cameron; the building is not located. Looked at before use: buildings strung along the foot of a wooded hill with mine dumps on its skyline; at the left a many-sided pavilion with two tall stacks behind it; a square hipped-roof building at the right; an open flat in the foreground. No caption or mark on the copy. Which way it looks has not been worked out.

name: Pinnacle Park (footbridge over the tracks)
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: The library: 'Railroad tracks running under ornate footbridge with wire fence alongside ... Two warmly dressed women are seated on a rock in the mid-ground.' Its caption says the park lay on both sides of parallel Midland Terminal and Short Line tracks, joined by this bridge. PPLD's rights line is a rightsstatements.org 'copyright not evaluated' statement; the owner's report of permission covers PPLD. Looked at before use: a single track runs under a timber footbridge of two arches with a tower at each end; at the left a wire-fenced enclosure with a pagoda-roofed shelter. Only one track shows in this view, though the library's caption speaks of parallel tracks. Reduced from the library's 4,200 px copy to 2,000 px. The library's own page says 'In Copyright - Educational Use' and asks that publication be requested; it is shown on the owner's report of permission.
